title: Flight management IMA/AFDX architecture - derived example requirements
coverage: Covers fms::fms.impl and its four module implementations, five function threads, typed exchanges, CPU/memory bindings, partition schedules, CAN/AFDX topology, six virtual links and explicit flows.
Only the active three-switch Actual_Connection_Binding configuration is in scope. Module roots are subviews of this one example, not independent requirement cases.
limitations: These requirements reproduce architectural declarations, not executable flight-management algorithms or proof of schedulability/network feasibility. Existing OSATE validation is not a pass.
The top-level flow latency bounds at fms.aadl lines 72-76 are comments and are not normative limits in this draft.
The alternative paths_specification annex refers to sw4 although sw4 is commented out; those contradictory routes are excluded rather than treated as requirements.
The physical-bandwidth and message-size literals in fms_hardware.aadl need unit/standard review; this draft does not promote them to AFDX requirements or silently substitute paper values.
The REAL annex invokes a restriction theorem but its local check is 1=1; its presence is not proof of ARINC653 compliance.

The author report identifies the same model family and depicts the four modules, but no commit identifier binds its diagrams, analysis assumptions or optimized network settings to this source revision.
original_requirement_status: An author-authored design/analysis report explicitly linked to the AADLib FMS was located. It is not a standalone, revision-matched original requirement set. The draft therefore remains entirely model_derived.

requirements.text: The FMS example shall contain four execution modules, one keyboard, one display, one remote data concentrator (RDC), one CAN bus, one physical AFDX network and three AFDX switch devices.

evidence.note: Active model declarations at the pinned source revision; no external standard-compliance claim is implied.

requirements.text: Module 1 shall host separate keyboard-unit (KU1) and multifunction-display (MFD1) processes; module 2 shall host the flight-manager (FM1) process; module 3 shall host an ADIRU process; and module 4 shall host a navigation-database (NDB) process.

requirements.text: Module 1 shall use a 50 ms ARINC653 major frame with a 25 ms KU1 partition slot followed by a 25 ms MFD1 partition slot, each marking a periodic-processing start.

requirements.text: The AFDX physical bus shall contain six virtual links named VL1 through VL6. All four modules, the RDC and each of the three switches shall expose accesses connected to the physical AFDX network.

requirements.text: The waypoint-identifier connection shall be bound to VL1; waypoint-information and ETA connections shall share VL2; database query shall use VL3; database answer shall use VL4; speed shall use VL5; and pressure shall use VL6.

requirements.text: VL1, VL2, VL3, VL4, VL5 and VL6 shall have declared bandwidth-allocation gaps of 32, 8, 16, 64, 32 and 32 ms respectively. Each shall retain the locally declared 1 ms latency-constraint property, which is a model input rather than an established traversal-time result.

requirements.text: For the active Actual_Connection_Binding route configuration, VL1 and VL4 shall follow sw1 then sw2; VL2 and VL3 shall follow sw2 then sw1; VL5 shall follow sw3, sw1, sw2; and VL6 shall use sw3.

requirements.text: The model shall expose five named inter-module end-to-end flows: waypoint identifier, waypoint information, database query, database answer and speed. It shall also expose the complete keyboard-request chain through module 1, module 2, module 4, module 2 and module 1 to the display.
